outline: 1388 Mental Shortcuts for Adding and Subtracting Integers

examples.question_text:
Evaluate each expression. Explain which operation you do first.
(a) $51-7 \times 6+8$
(b) $31-12+5$
examples.solution_text:
(a) Multiply before subtracting or adding.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}51-7 \times 6+8\\&=51-42+8\\&=9+8\\&=17\end{aligned}$
(b) Subtraction and addition have equal priority, so work from left to right.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}31-12+5\\&=19+5\\&=24\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text: Evaluate $84 \div 7 \times 3+11$. Explain why you divide before multiplying.
examples.solution_text:
Division and multiplication have equal priority. Read them from left to right, so divide $84$ by $7$ first.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}84 \div 7 \times 3+11\\&=12 \times 3+11\\&=36+11\\&=47\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text:
Evaluate both expressions. Explain how the brackets change the first operation.
(a) $5 \times (17-8)+14$
(b) $5 \times 17-8+14$
examples.solution_text:
(a) Do the subtraction inside the brackets first.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}5 \times (17-8)+14\\&=5 \times 9+14\\&=45+14\\&=59\end{aligned}$
(b) There are no brackets, so multiply before subtracting or adding.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}5 \times 17-8+14\\&=85-8+14\\&=77+14\\&=91\end{aligned}$
The brackets make $17-8$ a group that is worked out before multiplying.

examples.question_text:
A group buys $5$ tickets at $\$8$ each and $3$ maps at $\$7$ each.
Write a number sentence and find the total cost.
examples.solution_text:
Multiply to find each cost, then add the two costs.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}5 \times 8+3 \times 7\\&=40+3 \times 7\\&=40+21\\&=61\end{aligned}$
The total cost is $\$61$.

examples.question_text: Evaluate $80-30 \div 5+7$. Explain which operation you do first.
examples.solution_text:
Divide before subtracting or adding. Then work from left to right.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}80-30 \div 5+7\\&=80-6+7\\&=74+7\\&=81\end{aligned}$

examples.derivation: 7×6=42; 51−42=9; 9+8=17. Separately, 31−12=19; 19+5=24. These follow multiplication priority and left-to-right addition/subtraction.
84÷7=12; 12×3=36; 36+11=47. Division precedes multiplication here because equal-priority operations are evaluated left to right.
With brackets: 17−8=9; 5×9=45; 45+14=59. Without brackets: 5×17=85; 85−8=77; 77+14=91. The comparison correctly demonstrates how grouping changes the first operation.
Tickets cost 5×8=40 dollars; maps cost 3×7=21 dollars; 40+21=61 dollars. The number sentence represents both purchases and evaluates products before addition.
30÷5=6; 80−6=74; 74+7=81. Division is completed first, followed by subtraction and addition from left to right.
